issues.description: The problem statement UML and the template declare Farm.singFarmSong() as returning void, but the solution implementation returns a String. This return-type mismatch between the specification/template and the solution can confuse students about the expected signature and how the song should be produced (printed vs. returned).
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution with the problem/template by changing singFarmSong() in the solution to have a void return type and print the song directly (or alternatively update the problem statement and template to specify a String return if returning the song text is intended). Ensure all three artifacts use the same return type.

issues.description: The problem UML specifies a private method singFarmSongVerse(animal: Animal):void (i.e., it takes an Animal parameter and returns void), but the template's method signature has no parameter (private void singFarmSongVerse(/*Animal animal*/)) while the solution implements a method private String singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal) (different return type and uses the Animal parameter). The template's missing parameter and the solution's differing return type create a mismatch across artifacts.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template, problem statement, and solution consistent: either (A) change the template method signature to private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal) and implement printing (matching the UML), and update the solution to return void and print, or (B) update the UML and template to accept/return String if the intended design is to build and return the song text. Prefer aligning with the UML (void + Animal parameter) to avoid confusing students.
